turns.speaker: Nikhil

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil observed Sandip’s performance with a stillness that bordered on disapproval. He stated that Sandip’s attempts at theatricality were unnecessary and that he would not indulge in such displays, requesting that Sandip address the matter directly, if he had one to address.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip allowed his gaze to linger on Nikhil, a faint, almost imperceptible smile playing on his lips. turns.speaker: Nikhil

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip allowed his eyes to roam the room, pausing briefly on a collection of antique porcelain before returning their attention to Nikhil, a faint air of amusement coloring his tone as he suggested that perhaps the landowner’s insistence on clarity and directness was merely a convenient disguise for a certain… rigidity of thought, a condition, he mused, not entirely dissimilar to the limitations imposed by a particularly narrow-minded interpretation of Sanskrit prosody. turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil observed Sandip’s continued attempts at obfuscation with a weariness that settled deeper into his expression. turns.speaker: Sandip

turns.speaker: Bimala

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip permitted himself a small, almost mournful smile, his gaze drifting towards the ceiling as if seeking some celestial validation for his observations. turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil regarded Sandip with a steady gaze, his expression betraying neither agreement nor amusement. turns.speaker: Sandip

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala’s fingers traced the rim of her teacup, her gaze drifting towards the window where the late afternoon light cast long shadows across the lawn. turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip tilted his head, a languid gesture suggesting amused condescension, and remarked that a quiet strength, as Mrs. Bimala so elegantly phrased it, was often merely the prelude to a more… vigorous assertion of will, a phenomenon one observed frequently in the natural world, wouldn’t one agree, Nikhil? turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala raised her eyes slightly, a faint crease appearing between her brows as she regarded Sandip. turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip allowed a theatrical sigh to escape his lips, feigning a moment of profound contemplation before turning his gaze towards Nikhil. turns.speaker: Nikhil

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala’s fingers traced the rim of her teacup, her gaze fixed on the swirling liquid within. turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip let his gaze drift towards the window, as if contemplating some profound vista beyond the confines of the room, before turning back to address Nikhil with a carefully measured tone. opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip inquired of Bimala as to where she intended to flee, addressing her as Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip remarked to Nikhil that he questioned why Browning was not among his books, recalling a conversation with Bimala about a college contest involving Browning's translation, and asking if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip explained to Nikhil that he had managed to translate Browning into Bengali, though the result was far from a lasting joy for Bengal, and that he once believed himself on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened. opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip informed Bimala that it was pointless for her to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil had ceased reading poetry since his marriage, and that he suspected a return of his poetic inspiration.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip stated that Nikhil had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip inquired of Nikhil whether the warning concerned his poetic inspiration.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were agitated and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise flight.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil clarified to Sandip that he had come to provide information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip commented to Nikhil that a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, had the estates been his, and suggested that Nikhil's weakness was also undermining neighboring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil pointed out to Sandip that he had not offered advice, and requested that Sandip refrain from giving it, adding that it was futile. He then stated that he needed to inform Sandip that his followers had been secretly oppressing his tenantry, and demanded that he leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip questioned Nikhil, asking whether the threat was due to fear of the Mussulmans or some other apprehension.
